chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil and Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
"The two traders have the option [to cancel the deal] until they part, and the owner of the animal [has the option] for three days."

key_terms.الْبَائِعَانِ: The two traders/parties to the sale
key_terms.الْخِيَارِ: The option/right to choose to confirm or cancel the deal

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cancelling a sale contract in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) codifies the principle of 'khiyar al-majlis,' granting both buyer and seller the right to rescind a contract until they part ways, thereby ensuring mutual consent and preventing hasty decisions. It specifically distinguishes the sale of livestock by granting the buyer a three-day inspection period ('khiyar al-rawiya'), a ruling that highlights the Shia emphasis on protecting buyers from hidden defects in animals. This narration is foundational in the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* for establishing the flexibility and fairness inherent in Islamic commercial jurisprudence.
